note: Authored trail husbandry estimates informed by smallholding references, not measured 1848 yields. Adult milk animals are already in milk, with 180 days remaining; no breeding. Hens use finite scratching, shared leftover portions and grain. Cow/goat fodder fills pasture shortfalls. Yield allowances remain 8/2 lb milk and 0.5 egg before limitations. Prices and feed quantities are estimates. Table food retains exact calories and expiry. Egg progress is canonicalized before laying for stable save boundaries.

feeding.note: Nominal dry-ration and habitat allowances are calibration estimates. Sharing edible portions is off for new journeys; existing saved choices persist. When enabled it consumes actual portions before grain and protects the current human ration. Grain alone maintains energy but is not modeled as a complete laying ration. No dedicated mineral or body-size simulation. Pasture assessment supplies shared regional, seasonal and water inputs to oxen, mounts and dairy animals. Named grazing camps remove the habitat cap for one paid rest day, retaining seasonal and water limits. Dairy animals use explicit maintenance-plus-milk TDN budgets, dry-matter capacity and physical hay supplementation; the fractional surplus curve now applies only to hens. Cow/goat daily_feed_lb fields are legacy nominal allowances, not current requirements.

ruminants.note: Representative sizes and TDN energy budgets informed by extension examples, not measured trail diets. Cow maintenance proxy includes mid-pregnancy in its source; goat coefficients are approximations between different examples. Protein/minerals and feed spoilage are not simulated. Habitat/season are quantity caps, not nutrient percentages. Fodder is physical hay with explicit dry matter and TDN. Milk ceilings are unchanged.
